notes:
Replication title and authors verified against assigned reference. Description prioritised for selecting the average-person paired test; target_match=false records the explicit Table 10 locator conflict. Table 10 heart-attack likelihood instead prints F(3, 580) = 14.58 and p <.001 across four targets (N=584); these omnibus values were not merged with the pairwise test. Table 11 additionally prints Cohen’s d=-0.60, but requested test statistic retained. Table 8 prints average-person n=147, while Table 11 prints t(249); exact paired-test analytic n therefore left null. Authors describe this specific average-person result as supported, while their overall replication verdict is partial/mixed. Original statistics reproduced in the replication manuscript were not substituted for independently acquired original-paper evidence. Original acquisition: DOI 403; Unpaywall closed; OpenAlex no OA location; no full-text route in open search; ResearchGate alternative 403. No failed route retried.
Source follow-up: Fresh original-only extraction from the supplied published article. Title and authors match the assigned reference. The target-page scan was visually checked to validate the multivariate F statistic and p bound against embedded OCR. Analytic N is left null because it is not printed for the heart-attack MANOVA; no N was derived from degrees of freedom or substituted from enrollment, univariate Table 2, or individual conditions. The event-level MANOVA is distinct from Table 2 univariate tests and within-condition self–other pairwise tests. Replication and reported success are unassigned placeholders.
Completion source review (n_o): The Study 2 heart-attack self-versus-average-student comparison is in Group A. Visual inspection ties the Average student column to footnote b, which explicitly prints n = 25 for Group A. This is the condition-specific participant count for the within-condition self-other contrast; Group A total and other comparison-condition counts do not define this target. Exclusions are unspecified.
